title: A Safehouse for the Drop
premise: Lena Underhill, a crash investigator haunted by the death of her family in row twelve, receives a meeting invitation from a handler she knows is dead—and learns the crash was no accident, but the price of an extraction gone wrong. The defector, Marek Voss, carries proof of who ordered it, and every intelligence service that let row twelve burn now wants him silenced before dawn. As Lena moves him through the city's blind corridors toward a waiting flight, she discovers Marek may be bait designed to flush out the last person who knows the truth: her. In the end, Lena chooses love over duty—burning her own cover to put Marek on the plane and herself in the open, trading her invisibility for the truth about row twelve.
about_author: Orsen Sandoval is a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade reconstructing accident timelines before turning to fiction. He writes from a coastal town he refuses to name, drawing on his obsession with the small mechanical failures that hide human ones.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Opening on her insomnia ritual—replaying flight data of the crash that killed her family—we see her meticulous, hollow life. A sealed envelope arrives containing a meeting invitation signed by Handler Kessler, whom she buried two years ago. Emotional beat: grief cracked open by impossible hope.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Appointment
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She keeps the midnight meeting at a decommissioned transit depot, finding not Kessler but a dead-drop recording: Kessler's voice explaining the crash was engineered to cover a failed extraction, and naming her as the last living witness. A tail follows her home. Beat: terror braided with purpose.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Supposed to Land
chapters.summary: Marek's POV introduced. Hiding in a dockside flophouse, defector Marek Voss counts hours until his dawn flight, unaware his handlers have marked him expendable. He spots surveillance and bolts, colliding with Lena when both target the same safehouse address from Kessler's recording. Beat: wary alliance forged in adrenaline.

chapters.title: Terms of Extraction
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the safehouse, they trade truths: Marek has the ledger proving who sold out the original extraction; Lena realizes her family died to bury it. They plan a route to the airfield through the city's service tunnels. Beat: the cold arithmetic of survival begins to feel like trust.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Costs
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Deciphering the ledger, Lena finds her late husband's name—not as victim, but as a courier who unknowingly carried the evidence aboard. Her mourning curdles into betrayal and questions about everything she loved. Beat: the past rewritten, grief weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Tunnel Music
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. The tunnel run goes wrong when a maintenance crew turns out to be hunters; a chase through flooded conduits costs them their radio and nearly Marek's life. Lena drags him out through a storm grate. Beat: dependence deepening into something neither will name yet.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Recovering in a church basement, Lena confronts the possibility Kessler's message itself was the trap—that Marek is bait to draw out whoever still holds the ledger's missing page. She tests him; he passes, then admits he suspected her first. Beat: love and suspicion forced to share a room.

chapters.title: Dawn Is a Deadline
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With three hours to the flight, the hunters close the net, and Lena discovers the extraction pilot is compromised—the same man who signed off on row twelve. She must choose: abort and vanish forever, or board the plane carrying the truth and the traitor. Beat: duty and desire collide.

chapters.title: Flight Plan
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Climax on the tarmac: Lena boards, exposes the pilot mid-taxi, and forces the plane down while Marek broadcasts the ledger to every news desk he can reach. Gunfire across the runway; Lena takes a bullet shielding Marek. Beat: sacrifice made visible, truth made unstoppable.

chapters.title: A Safehouse for the Drop
chapters.summary: Marek's POV, closing. Weeks later, in a real safehouse by the sea, Lena recovers as the hearings begin and row twelve finally gets its true record. Marek asks what she'll do now that invisibility is gone. She answers: live loudly. Beat: grief transmuted into a future chosen together.
